newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schwarz Pharma 96 sales jump, growth seen.
newsitem.headline: Schwarz Pharma 96 sales jump, growth seen.

text.p: German drugs group Schwarz Pharma AG on Wednesday said strong U.S. sales helped boost total group turnover by 17.5 percent in 1996 and should spark more sales and profits growth this year.
In a mandatory bourse statement the family-owned group reported 1996 group sales jumped to 1.19 billion marks ($719.9 million), topping an earlier 1.18 billion-mark sales forecast.
Looking ahead, the group said: "We are optimistic about the year that has just begun. Group sales should climb by six to eight percent and profits should grow even more strongly."
Last year foreign sales, which for the first time outpaced sales at home, rose 26 percent to 614 million marks while domestic sales climbed 9.7 percent to 581 million marks, the group said.
Sales in the U.S., where Schwarz Pharma has been expanding aggressively with numerous marketing and sales joint-ventures, surged by 44 percent to 266 million marks.
The group declined to give exact profit figures but said it was very likely the group would be able to reach its forecast DVFA result of 4.30 marks per share.
More details will be released on April 16.
Mirroring other German drugs' groups forecasts, Schwarz Pharma predicted foreign sales would again be a growth engine this year with domestic sales remaining more sluggish.
Companies have faced soft German economic growth as well as restrictive health care budgets which have prompted doctors to prescribe cheaper drugs, cutting into companies' sales.
The group also said it plans to continue expanding its market share in key drugs markets.
Shares in Schwarz Pharma, which have been a market favourite since the group floated its shares in 1995, vaulted 3.51 percent higher to 118 marks in pre-bourse IBIS trading on the news.
The broader IBIS DAX index was down 0.54 percent.
